item.title: Stellwerk 0.31.0
item.description:
Minor Changes

  • #144 `6af9aca` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: the Mac notices when its line to OpenAI stalls or breaks, reconnects, holds actions while it can't hear „Stopp“ and tells you what didn't arrive; the apps show Mac reconnecting… / Reconnecting… and keep the call through network drops of up to 15 s.
  • #139 `e66fd9c` Thanks @grischaerbe! - The Front Desk can now approve a plan waiting for approval or send what to change in it, after telling you what the plan says (other blocked actions still stay in the app). A plan that arrives counts as waiting for approval in the Front Desk's queue until it's decided, not as a finished turn, and nothing else goes to that chat by voice meanwhile. The Front Desk can also let an agent fix a failed setup script, like "Fix" in the app. It starts new workspaces on an open pull request or a branch, and with the agent, model, effort or plan mode you ask for (plan mode only with Claude Code). A branch that already has a workspace gets that workspace; a pull request from a fork, a branch that doesn't exist and one checked out outside Stellwerk are refused. It can list a project's open pull requests and branches to start from. "Work on PR" no longer shows a fork's pull request as already having a workspace because its branch has the same name as one of yours. A plan too long to be read whole is approved in the app only (changes still go by voice). Nothing goes by voice to a chat whose agent waits for an answer to its question: the Front Desk answers it or uses a new chat. When checking out an existing branch for a new workspace fails, trying again (by voice or with "Work on PR") checks it out again instead of opening the failed workspace. A branch counts as existing on the remote only under its full name, and searching pull requests and branches by voice also finds older ones.
  • #144 `6af9aca` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: news and action results wait for a real pause instead of talking over you; instructions aren't cut off mid-sentence, and „Äh ne, Moment, ich meinte …“ holds what was about to go out.
  • #139 `e66fd9c` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: ask it to show you a chat ("zeig mir den Chat", "mach den Workspace auf") and it opens that chat on the device the call runs on, on iPhone, iPad, Android and in the Mac window (also one connected to another Mac), as a chat link would: the chat you name, else the one its request is about, else the one active last. The call card goes down to its bar so the chat shows; the Mac opens its Stellwerk window. With the phone locked or the app in the background it opens once the app is in front, and the voice says so. Only the device with the call opens it, and nothing opens again after the call moves to another device, also when the device was locked or offline while it moved. When the device doesn't confirm, the voice says it couldn't confirm the chat opened. Apps from before this can't, and the voice says so; chats of archived workspaces don't open.
  • #139 `e66fd9c` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: while an agent works, an instruction or question by voice still waits in the chat's queue, but it can now also go right into the running turn, as Send now does in the apps ("schick's ihm sofort", or a correction of what the agent is doing). The voice says which one it does; when it's unclear, it asks "direkt oder in die Warteschlange?". Two messages sent to an idle chat at the same moment no longer start two turns side by side: the second goes into the turn the first started.
  • #143 `a8c3a78` Thanks @fabifink! - Agents can offer a Google Cloud sign-in in the chat: when gcloud or Google's client libraries need one, the agent's reply shows a "Sign in to Google Cloud" button on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android. One sign-in renews both the gcloud CLI and the client libraries, from whatever device you're on: copy the code Google shows and come back, and Stellwerk takes it from the clipboard and finishes (in the window on the Mac that runs the agents there's no code at all). Afterwards it tells the chat, so the agent carries on by itself. The Mac window's Settings → Account now shows the Mac's Google Cloud sign-ins too, with Sign in and Renew.
  • #147 `961fc80` Thanks @kaptnkoala! - Mac: right-click a file or folder in All files, or a file in Changes, for Conductor's menu: Open in (Finder, editors, terminals; 1–9 pick the first nine), Copy path and Copy relative path. Changes adds View and Discard changes, which puts the file back to how it is on the target branch (a new one goes into the Trash) after asking. Open in also knows Rider and PhpStorm.
  • #151 `8dc26ef` Thanks @GarreltMock! - Sections in the project list: group projects into your own sections such as "Work" and "Private", each with an optional emoji and a header in small caps that a click folds. Projects in no section stay on top as before, so nothing changes without sections. On the Mac, a section's ⋯ (on hover) or right-click adds a project to it and makes, edits or deletes sections; "New Section…" is also in "Add Project", in a right-click on the sidebar and in a project's "Move to Section". Projects and sections are dragged into place. iPhone, iPad and Android show and fold the sections and move projects with "Move to Section" in a project's long-press menu.
  • #138 `e4fc1ad` Thanks @fabifink! - The Operator is gone: no more Operator row, to-do list or chat on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android, and no Settings → Operator page. The Front Desk row now sits at the top of the list. Hosts tell older apps the Operator is off, so they hide it too.
  • #146 `4a6ef10` Thanks @kaptnkoala! - `stellwerk://workspace/<id>` opens a workspace with its last chat on whichever paired Mac has it, on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android, the way `stellwerk://chat/<id>` opens a chat. An optional `session=<chat id>` opens it on that chat (a closed one comes back as a tab), so Conductor's `workspace?id=…&session=…` form works too. Agents know the id as `$STELLWERK_WORKSPACE_ID`, so a task board can link to where an agent works on a task. An archived workspace isn't restored by the link: the app says it's archived on that Mac.

    • Patch Changes

  • #150 `2c66864` Thanks @grischaerbe! - The pills over the message box (subagents, background commands, wakeups) wrap onto more lines when there are many, instead of running off the side, on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android.
  • #148 `4b06d70` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: Settings → Front Desk → Longest call also offers 2 and 4 hours, beside 10 to 60 minutes. The default stays 20 minutes; the voice still wraps up a minute before the limit.
  • #144 `6af9aca` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: the voice no longer reads out the brain's notes, and the brain corrects what the voice promised before its answer.
  • #149 `e4e54e5` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: during a Front Desk call, pressing the AirPods' stem (or a Beats' button) mutes and unmutes the microphone, like the call window's Mute. The iPhone already does this through CallKit; Android has no such gesture for apps. Hanging up by pressing twice isn't possible on the Mac (macOS brings up Siri instead).
  • #140 `de32143` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: the right panel's Changes, All files and Checks tabs are always there, in that order. They no longer close (the × that came up on hover covered the end of the tab's title or count), and the "+" for reopening them is gone.
  • #145 `66ff8f0` Thanks @grischaerbe! - A question the agent asks while starting a background subagent (or making another call at the same time) no longer disappears: the chat keeps waiting for your answer instead of showing "working" forever. Writing a message instead of answering a question now reaches the agent: the question is turned down and the message goes into the running turn, for Claude Code, Codex and Pi.

item.title: Stellwerk 0.30.0
item.description:
Minor Changes

  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Android: notifications through Firebase when an agent finishes, fails or asks, like on the iPhone. They need a release built with Firebase and, on each Mac with agents, its Firebase service account in Settings → Devices → Android notifications; Send test there reaches Android phones too.
  • #135 `7b253e6` Thanks @GarreltMock! - Pills over the message box: what a chat's agent has going besides its turn shows as a pill each, a robot for a subagent, a terminal for a background command or a process it left running (`npm run dev &`), an alarm clock for a planned wakeup. Each has Stop; a subagent's pill opens its live log (prompt, messages, tool calls), on the Mac in a tab next to the chats, on iPhone, iPad and Android as a sheet. A chat whose subagents still work after its turn stays working (and notifies only once they're done): like a running agent it holds back Merge, rewinding and archiving without Stop; the message box's Stop (during the turn or after) stops them. The workspace lists show the time in blue while a background process or run script runs, and an alarm clock for a wakeup. Archiving or closing the chat ends everything. A wakeup no longer leaves its chat stuck on working after it ran. Based on #98 and #105.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Android: the Front Desk calls with a full-screen call notification (on Android 14 and newer allow Full-screen calls in Settings → Front Desk) and can be called from its row; the call is the same green card and bar as on the iPhone, with an Audio menu for Bluetooth and headphones on Android 12 and newer. While the Front Desk is on, an ongoing notification per Mac shows the same card (the counts, a question with its options or a finished turn's suggested replies as buttons, or the newest rows) and sounds for a finished turn, a question, a blocked action or a plan, in place of their notifications, as long as notifications and its "Front Desk" channel are on. Where it differs from the iPhone: Call is a button only where the options leave room, there are at most three buttons, the recommended option can't stand out, the rows can't be tapped one by one, and a swiped notification comes back silently with the next change. Calls ring with the app closed only in builds with Firebase.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - iPhone and iPad: the Front Desk calls like a phone call (CallKit, also with the app closed and on the lock screen; calls show up in the Phone app's Recents, and a tap there calls that Mac again) and can be called from its row; the call is a green card you drag down into a bar while you use the app, with Mute, Speaker (Audio with AirPods, headphones or CarPlay around, like in the Phone app) and Hang up. While the Front Desk is on, the iPhone has a Live Activity on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island: how many workspaces work, which turns finished unseen and what waits, then a question with up to four options as buttons (the recommended one green), a finished turn's decision question with suggested replies, or the newest rows, and one round Call button. A finished turn, a question, a blocked action or a plan makes it sound like a notification, and in return the iPhone gets no agent notifications for them while the Front Desk is on. Swiped away, it comes back with the next news; after an app update it's back once the app was opened; it renews itself before iOS ends it after 8 hours. Calls ring with the app closed on TestFlight, App Store and ad hoc builds; debug builds ring only while the app is open and say so in Settings. When Apple refuses an iPhone's Live Activity token, Settings → Devices on the Mac says so and that reinstalling the app gets a new one.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk on the Mac: the Front Desk row under the Operator starts a call; the call is a small green window that floats over everything (in all Spaces, movable), rings with Answer and Decline, hangs up with ✕, ⌘W or ⎋ and mutes with ⌘⇧M, also when the main window is closed. Settings → Front Desk (off by default) has the OpenAI key, the voice, the brain (agent, model and effort; Sonnet with low effort by default), the summaries' model, the longest call and the silence after which it hangs up, calls per hour, raise urgency after, bundle requests within, quiet hours (one window, the same every day), the typing sound you hear while it works (once it starts, at least 2.5 s, so it's never just a click), and whether the window may use the microphone. Below: Style (the text that comes with the app, editable, Reset brings it back), Memory (one entry per line; add, edit, delete), Rules (the fixed rules of the voice and the brain, read-only), Queue (each request with why the Front Desk would or wouldn't call now, and the ones removed lately with the reason) and Recent calls (the last 20 with the seconds OpenAI billed, the Summary written after each, the Transcript, the call's Log and, for a call that rang, what became of its ring push). A `stellwerk://frontdesk` link from a web page or another app asks before it starts a call or takes one over to the Mac's microphone; answering the call that rings goes through at once.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - The Front Desk has a name, Pam unless you change it (Mac: Settings → Front Desk → Name; empty for none): its calls show "Pam – Front Desk" on iPhone (CallKit and the call card), Android (call notification and card) and in the Mac's call window, iOS's Recents lists the call as "Pam", and the voice introduces itself with the name and answers to it.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: a voice assistant you call, and that calls you, about what your workspaces need. Turn it on in Settings → Front Desk on the Mac and add an OpenAI API key (kept in the Mac's Keychain). A call runs on OpenAI's GPT-Live (German, voice Nuri by default, about $0.05 a minute), with the audio going straight between your device and OpenAI; the Mac follows the call and hands everything to look up or do to a brain, a Claude or Codex process with only the Front Desk's tools: reading a chat or a diff, answering an agent's question, sending an instruction to exactly the chat you talk about, opening a new chat in a workspace for a new task, the git bar's actions that destroy nothing, stopping an agent, archiving when nothing is left, a new workspace, asking an agent and telling you what its answer means for your question, "call me when …", and searching your chats and earlier calls. The host keeps one request per workspace (a question, a finished or failed turn, red checks, a blocked action or plan, an agent that wants to talk); an open question keeps its place while another chat of that workspace finishes, which comes after it. A call opens with what's up, goes straight into the most urgent topic and mentions finished turns briefly as news; what a call you heard already told you isn't told again. An action is announced first and goes out 3 seconds after the voice said it unless you say "Stopp"; hanging up after you heard it sends it, and the voice confirms what really happened. When you ask an agent something during a call, the brain gets the agent's whole answer and sums up what matters for your question; while it waits, the voice fills a silence with a short "I'm on it", and after two minutes without a summary you hear the answer as written. After a call, a short protocol of what was decided goes into the next day's calls; lasting preferences go into its memory, and how it talks is a style you can change. For urgent requests it calls you: at most 3 times an hour by default, bundled, never in quiet hours, never twice for the same request. It rings on every paired phone and every Mac window, and tapping the row on another device takes the call over. Agents started while it's on can ask for a call themselves (`request_call` in the Stellwerk skill).

    • Patch Changes

  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - iPhone, iPad, Android and the Mac window: the Operator row, Search and the team chats no longer stay missing when the app's first look at a Mac's agents failed (the Mac app's own host still starting, a Mac out of reach); the app asks again until the Mac answers.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Android: hanging up a Front Desk call no longer posts the call notification again after the call's service stopped (which Android can refuse with a crash, or leave behind).
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Android: reopening the app after Android ended it in the background, or from Recents, no longer runs the link or call notification it was first opened with again (which could start a Front Desk call or answer a long-gone one by itself).
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Android: the app no longer lists the Bluetooth permission it never asked for; Front Desk calls still go to Bluetooth headphones.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Android: the notification, microphone and local network questions come one after another, so the microphone question is no longer lost (and read as "denied") when the notification question is open.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - A malformed built-in push key is an error instead of something the Mac works around: building Stellwerk (also Install from source) fails with "APNs key in this build is malformed: …" when the key isn't a single PKCS#8 P-256 key or its key ID or team ID isn't 10 letters and digits, and a build that has such a key anyway says so at start in the host log and in Settings → Devices → Push notifications, and sends no pushes to iPhones. The host log now has a line with Apple's answer for every push (its status, the apns-id and the reason when it refuses, never the token), and a push to Apple that hangs counts as failed after 10 seconds.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - A Codex helper agent (the Front Desk's brain) always runs read-only: when Codex's managed config doesn't allow the read-only sandbox, it doesn't start, with a message saying so, instead of running with a sandbox that can write.
  • #131 `6d0eeab` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Workspaces in a new, empty repository (just created on GitHub, or `git init` without a commit) no longer fail with "git worktree failed (128): fatal: invalid reference: HEAD". The first workspace gives the repository an empty "Initial commit" on its default branch and pushes it, so pull requests have a base; files already lying in the checkout stay untracked. When the remote can't be reached or the push fails, the workspace says so and the next one tries again; when someone published a first commit meanwhile, it starts from theirs.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk on Android: a call answered on the lock screen no longer shows the app when it's minimized; minimizing asks to unlock first, and without the unlock the call stays on screen.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: after a question to an agent in a call, the voice says its answer comes "gleich" instead of "später", which sounded like a long wait.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: an agent's answer to a question that comes while the call moves to another device isn't lost if the call ends before the move is done: it becomes a request in the queue, as when the call ends before the voice got it.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: an answer given in a call only goes to the question the user decided. If the chat asks another question by the time it goes out (the first answered in the app, then a new one), the voice says it didn't go out instead of answering a question the user never heard.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: an opened call log in Settings → Front Desk → Recent calls no longer redraws with every change on the host while agents work, and lays out its entries once instead of as they scroll into view, so reading a log for a while no longer hangs the window.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk, from a call with two chats working in one workspace:
  • Whatever comes in during a call is told in it: a chat's result no longer disappears unheard because its chat counts as read or works again before the voice got to it.
  • Each chat has its own title. The voice no longer announces one chat's result under the other chat's subject; the workspace keeps one profile.
  • When a chat's agent goes on by itself (a background task finished), the voice no longer says "done"; it learns the chat works on.
  • Actions said together (the same instruction to two chats) are confirmed together, with one word, instead of each result read out in full.
  • iPhone, Android and the Mac window: switching to another chat tells the Mac the previous one isn't shown any more, so its next replies count as unread again (they were counted as read for good).
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: the voice no longer hears "done in the app" about what it did itself, and does hear it about what the user did. Whether a request it knew left by its own doing now follows from why the request left and what the voice's actions actually did once they went out (a message to that very chat, a merge, archiving), instead of a guess made when the action was announced. Asking an agent something, starting a review or a new chat no longer comes back as "done in the app", and an action held with "Stopp" no longer hides what happened meanwhile.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: asked to hang up („leg auf“, „das war's, tschüss“), the call now ends. The voice had no way to end it and only said it would; now the brain gets an `end_call` tool, its answer is the goodbye, and the host hangs up a few seconds after it.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac and Android: with the Front Desk off, the apps no longer look after it in the background. The Mac app holds no second change feed and no 15-second polling for it (also when its window shows another Mac), and Android stops its 15-second check, as the iPhone already did.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: a git action by voice without a chat (pull, automerge, ready for review …) no longer takes red checks or a failed setup out of the queue; only a push takes red checks with it, merging and archiving everything. Before, such an action dropped the entry while the checks stayed red, and nothing reported them again.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: when the line to OpenAI drops and its hang-up is slow, a call the user starts meanwhile no longer ends with it.
  • #130 `90d4221` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: a Front Desk call over AirPods or another Bluetooth headset no longer plays the voice slow and low. The call opens the headset's microphone first and waits for it to switch to headset mode before the voice plays; the call log says how it went.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk on iPhone and Android: a call answered while the system asks for the microphone doesn't start once that's allowed if the ringing ended meanwhile (answered elsewhere, timed out) or another call began to ring.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: a request that comes in during a call is told to the voice once, also when two queue changes come at the same moment.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: an order in a call is said once. GPT-Live's automatic acknowledgement, which retold the order before the Front Desk announced it, is off; the voice puts no "Mach ich." before the announcement and says nothing (not even "Bin dran.") until the action went out, so its confirmation stays one word. "Bin dran." for an agent's answer only comes when its summary takes longer than 3 s.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - The Front Desk's question with answer buttons (on the card and the lock screen) is short and stands on its own: one sentence, mostly under 80 characters, that says what it is about instead of pointing at the agent's text ("die Punkte unter „Hoch“", "mein Vorschlag"), without lead-in or reasons, the important part first, so it is clear without the chat.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Settings → Front Desk → Queue shows the decision question a finished turn put on the phones, with its buttons and what each sends, in the request's details, and keeps it under "Recently removed" once the request is gone, so a question that got replaced can still be read.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: when it reads a chat, the newest message and a message it looks up from a search come in whole, so it can tell you what an agent reported without asking the agent again. Older messages keep 1,500 characters instead of 800, and a long one loses its middle instead of its end, so its start and its conclusion stay.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: every chat gets its own entry in the queue. With several chats in one workspace, a chat that finished while another was still working used to vanish from the queue at once, and only the last chat to finish was reported. Now each chat's finished turn, question or call request stays until that chat is read, answered or works again, beside the other chats' entries; the workspace's title and profile stay shared. Red checks and a failed setup stay one entry for the workspace. The voice's `done`, `later` and `dismiss` take the chat when a workspace has more than one entry.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: a turn that only takes in a background task's progress is no finished turn and doesn't fire "call me when it's done"; removing the OpenAI key or the Firebase service account says so when the Keychain refuses, and a key read while it changes doesn't come back from the cache; a call's ring report goes only to the Mac it came from, on iPhone, iPad and Android.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk, from the PR review:
  • Android 8–11: the card's answer and reply buttons no longer act from the lock screen; they ask to unlock first (Android 12+ and iOS already did).
  • The call bar's green is darker on iPhone, Mac and Android, so its white text and icons are readable (6.2:1 instead of 2.6:1).
  • Android: the call report to the Mac is sent again after a brief 502–504 on the way, and saving it can no longer lose a newer report.
  • The build's push key check also rejects a key without the private key in it.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: ticking off, dismissing or postponing in a call no longer removes a request the user hasn't heard of. If a chat's question replaced the news being talked about, the brain is told what's there now and settles it only after that.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: an action in a call is confirmed with one word ("Erledigt.", "Läuft.") when nothing came between its announcement and its outcome; the full sentence with the workspace only follows when something did. The announcement leaves out the workspace being talked about, and the voice no longer repeats a stray example sentence ("Der Push-Fix hat die Anweisung.").
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: the Front Desk's switch moved from Settings → Front Desk to Settings → Experimental, and Settings → Front Desk (with all its other settings, now without a switch) is only there while the Front Desk is on.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: an action that a timed-out brain turn still scheduled no longer goes out. The voice had already said the turn failed, yet such an action went out with the next announcement or after two minutes; now it's held at once, until the next turn reaches the brain.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: two chats that share a title (both inherited the workspace's one) now get titles of their own instead of keeping the shared one. And when the call says goodbye after a silence and you speak up ("wait, stay"), it stays on the line instead of hanging up.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: the brain's tools know the call again. Each call started with them forgetting the last call and the running one, so the queue and workspace lists didn't mark what the user already knew, and `search` and `recent_calls` could return what was just said in the running call.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Front Desk: open a workspace during a call and its request leaves the queue quietly; the voice no longer says it's done.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - `scripts/install-ios.sh --adhoc` builds a release of the iOS app for ad hoc distribution and installs it, so a local build gets notifications, Live Activities and Front Desk calls with the app closed. Without `Config/Signing.local.xcconfig` the script explains how to set the team instead of exiting without a word.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: picking another Brain model in Settings → Front Desk switches the effort to one the model offers, as the Summaries row does, instead of keeping one the page then shows blank.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: Settings → Front Desk's Queue, Memory and Style no longer redraw with every change on the host while agents work, and a ringing call's panel and ring no longer wait for an open alert to close.
  • #134 `ea0c8ed` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: the ring that turns around a workspace's icon while an agent works is now the sidebar's muted gray, as Conductor draws its working loader, instead of the theme's accent (beige, black, yellow or lime by theme). It suits every color theme and leaves the colors to the pull request icon.
  • #134 `ea0c8ed` Thanks @grischaerbe! - The pull request icon in the workspace lists (iPhone, iPad, Android, the Mac window's sidebar) now follows Conductor's sidebar: it shows the PR as GitHub has it, whatever the checkout does (behind, ahead, uncommitted files). Green with the arrow when GitHub can merge it, a red X for failing checks, and new: the draft glyph for drafts, Conductor's conflict glyph in its highlight color for merge conflicts, and the merge queue in yellow, each with its words under the name ("Draft PR", "Merge conflict", "In merge queue"). The git bar's header still names the next step in the checkout first ("Behind by 1 commit" with Pull). Older apps keep the coarse colors; the host sends the finer state in a new optional field.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - A Mac build without the built-in push key now says so in the host log at launch (notifications, the Front Desk's calls and its card on iPhones are off then), and `scripts/install-host.sh` builds with the installed app's push key when none is given, like Install from source does.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Push: a phone that registers again replaces its earlier registration of the same kind on the Mac instead of adding a second one, so an iPhone that went from a debug build to a release build no longer keeps its old token; duplicates already in the Mac's device list are dropped.
  • #133 `e2fe4af` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: removing a project in Settings archives its open workspaces too, so it leaves the sidebar at once instead of moving to its end. The dialog names the workspaces with work still in them (chats working, uncommitted files, commits not pushed); archiving keeps their changes and commits (not ignored files), and restoring one from Search brings the project back.
  • `472bb55` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Test devices: the push when an agent hands a device over goes out like the agents' notifications, so it reaches Android phones with Firebase too.
  • #132 `64ad3e2` Thanks @GarreltMock! - Test devices, from a review:
  • `dh wait` on a device another agent holds ends once that agent lets it go, instead of waiting out its 20 minutes.
  • Text typed through adb (no stream) can no longer run commands on the device: a newline or `;` in it stays text.
  • Mac: clearing a device's alias and notes in Settings → Test devices while it isn't plugged in saves without an error.

item.title: Stellwerk 0.29.0
item.description:
Minor Changes

  • #118 `2fea7ff` Thanks @fabifink! - Test devices: Android phones and emulators on the Mac, shared by agents and people. Settings → Test devices on the Mac installs what's missing (adb, scrcpy) and names each device; iPhone, iPad and Android list them above the projects and show a device live, with touch, typing with the phone's keyboard, take over and notes. Agents drive them with `dh` and the bundled android-devices skill. A note someone leaves at a device, or a device handed back, arrives in the agent's chat, and an agent handing a device over sends a push.

    • Patch Changes

  • #127 `dbc0bf4` Thanks @kaptnkoala! - Mac: tables in a reply are part of its text, so a selection runs across cells, rows and the text around them; copied, cells come out separated by tabs and rows by line breaks, ready to paste into a spreadsheet. Tables with images in them can still only be selected cell by cell. On iPhone, iPad and Android tables stay as they were.

item.title: Stellwerk 0.28.0
item.description:
Minor Changes

  • #119 `3058c1d` Thanks @kaptnkoala! - Files in replies open in Stellwerk: links to files (relative, absolute, `<…>`, `file://`, with `:42` or `#L42`), inline code and paths in the text (`.context/plan.md`, `src/foo.ts:12`) become clickable when the host finds the file in the workspace. On the Mac they open in the tab next to the chats (Markdown rendered) instead of failing with "Das Programm kann nicht geöffnet werden. -50"; on iPhone, iPad and Android in a preview. All files now lists `.context` too.
  • #113 `bf71cf1` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Workspaces can be pinned above the projects and renamed: right-click on the Mac, swipe or long-press on iPhone and iPad, long-press on Android.

    • Patch Changes

  • #117 `34cbc2b` Thanks @fabifink! - Mac: the host no longer stops answering for hours (phones and other Macs couldn't connect, the window couldn't send) when many tools ran at once. git, gh, Tailscale, Entire and the helper calls (Operator line, branch name, new topic) now wait on threads of their own, and the project list asks git outside the database. A stalled host now says so in the host log until it's over, including a refused connection, and writes where its threads wait into `stall-<date>.txt` beside the log.
  • #114 `c7af186` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Settings → Devices: "Name on the phone" is now "Host name". It names this Mac at the top left of the Stellwerk window too, and a rename shows there and in the apps as soon as you press Return or leave the field, instead of on the next reconnect.
  • #116 `d392d3f` Thanks @GarreltMock! - Mac: a click on an image in a chat opens the viewer with all of the chat's images again (the strip at the bottom, the arrows and ← →), not just that one.
  • #121 `6879a0a` Thanks @GarreltMock! - On a team host, Settings → Devices lists only your own phones and Macs, and you can no longer remove someone else's. A malformed video request can no longer crash the host. Android build tools updated.
  • #126 `b933b5f` Thanks @GarreltMock! - Team host: a message written while someone else's turn runs no longer goes into that turn (it would run on their Claude account). It waits in the queue without Send now, and starts a turn of your own when theirs ends. The same on iPhone, Android and the Mac.
  • #123 `3de3c37` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: the chat tabs no longer show the wide system scroll bar when a mouse is connected. When the tabs don't fit, a thin bar like the one in the chat shows while you scroll and then fades out. The tabs in Search use the same bar.
  • #124 `5e7ce50` Thanks @GarreltMock! - An archive or run script that a workspace changed in its own settings (so an agent may have written it) now runs only after you allow it: iPhone, iPad, Android and the Mac ask "Run the changed archive script?" or "Run the changed run script?", and remember the answer per project and command. On team hosts, a device that hasn't signed in no longer sees who is typing or looking at which chat. Release builds now use the Swift package versions committed in `Package.resolved`.

item.title: Stellwerk 0.27.0
item.description:
Minor Changes

  • #110 `490b860` Thanks @GarreltMock! - "New project…" next to "Open project…" and "Clone from GitHub…" (Mac, iPhone, iPad, Android): a name and a parent folder on the Mac (default ~/stellwerk/repos), and Stellwerk makes the folder with git and a first commit, optionally a private GitHub repository with gh, and adds it as a project.
  • #100 `f1abce9` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Several run scripts per repository (`[scripts.run.<name>]` with `command`, a lucide `icon` and `default`, as Conductor has them): the Mac's Run tab lists them, each with Run, Stop once it has been up a second, and Open once it printed a local address, plus its own terminal; each runs on its own port. Settings → project → Run scripts edits them with an icon picker. iPhone, iPad and Android show the running and failed ones over the chat and all of them under "…" → Run scripts. While a run script runs, the workspace's time in the workspace lists is in Conductor's activity blue, on every app, and the Mac's Run tab has a blue dot. `run_mode` is gone: run scripts always run side by side.
  • #101 `d86c7cf` Thanks @GarreltMock! - Team host: one Mac shared by a small team. Choose "Team host" in the setup or Settings → Devices; each person pairs and signs in with GitHub (and Claude) on their phone or Mac. Messages show who wrote them, chats and workspaces who takes part, the message box who is typing. A turn runs on the Claude login, git author, GitHub token and gcloud config of the person who wrote it, with the chat's other people as co-authors; new branches carry their prefix, notifications go only to people in the chat. The Tailscale Serve port is a setting, so several macOS users can each run a host on one Mac. iOS, Android and the Mac window alike. A signed-in Mac pairs further phones as the same person (Settings → Account → Pair a phone), and the host reads GitHub with its people's sign-ins, so a bot account is optional.

    • Patch Changes

  • #95 `06a63ea` Thanks @grischaerbe! - A workspace's setup script runs before its agent starts: the first prompt (and anything sent meanwhile, also after unarchiving) waits in the chat's queue until setup is done, failed or stopped, so the agent no longer runs setup steps of its own alongside it.
  • #92 `bad510f` Thanks @GarreltMock! - Mac dashboards: back at the top of the sidebar under Search, with the page's favicon (the picked icon when it has none) and their ⌘⌥ shortcut at the row's end.
  • #104 `37ebf0e` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Diffs: a long line scrolls sideways instead of being cut off on the Mac or wrapped on iPhone and iPad, as on Android.
  • #102 `8e895ab` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Fable 5.2 in the model picker, right after Opus 5.5; Fable 5.1 stays further down for chats that use it.
  • #112 `614a24e` Thanks @GarreltMock! - The Mac host closes each git call's pipes as soon as git is done instead of a minute or two later: with many workspaces and terminals it held thousands of files open and ran into "Too many open files", and phones and the window couldn't reach it.
  • #96 `87d10e5` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: a `stellwerk://` link, from a dashboard or elsewhere, no longer sends Stellwerk to the background while the window is open.
  • #108 `e617c67` Thanks @GarreltMock! - Mac: the sidebar, the right panel and the Setup / Run logs have no fixed maximum anymore; they grow as far as the chat keeps its minimum width (and the panel's top its minimum height), as in Conductor.
  • #106 `be76e17` Thanks @GarreltMock! - When Claude only wakes up for a line from a Monitor, its end no longer sends a "finished" notification for every line.
  • #97 `41c648c` Thanks @GarreltMock! - iPhone notifications: "Only for messages from the phone" works again. Messages typed in a Mac's Stellwerk window no longer count as the phone's, and the Operator's work counts only when the phone asked for it.
  • #112 `614a24e` Thanks @GarreltMock! - The Mac host raises its open-file limit at launch, so big projects no longer fail with "Too many open files".
  • #112 `614a24e` Thanks @GarreltMock! - The host log names its open files and the limit at start, and notes when they pass half or most of the limit (and when they're back down), so a leak shows before "Too many open files".
  • #107 `2ccdc8b` Thanks @GarreltMock! - PR badge shows the pull request of the branch checked out now: when an agent switches to a new branch, the workspace follows it instead of keeping its first branch's PR.
  • #94 `8d5a637` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: pressing the PR button (Create PR, Merge, …) shows a spinner in the icon's color and size in its place; the icon no longer just vanishes for a moment on the light Create PR button.
  • #109 `a4ff3b6` Thanks @GarreltMock! - Mac: the default color theme is called Stellwerk instead of Conductor, and the Run tab, run script settings and "Ask agent" prompts name `$STELLWERK_PORT` / `$STELLWERK_ROOT_PATH` instead of the `CONDUCTOR_*` ones (both are still set). Stellwerk's own types drop the old name (`StellwerkDB`, `StellwerkColor`, `Host/Store`).
  • #99 `f76b7a4` Thanks @grischaerbe! - iPhone and Android: the setup script's row over the chat shows only while the script runs or after it failed, no longer "Completed setup script" for good. On iPhone the row now has a background, so the chat no longer shows through it. The setup log stays in the "…" menu.
  • #103 `f8454c2` Thanks @grischaerbe! - Mac: text pasted after an attachment in the message box (⌘V, or dictated with apps like Wispr Flow that paste) is sent again. Only the attachment reached the agent.
